text: Earth once had six kinds of humans, at the same time.
Not apes, humans, six different branches of us.
Today, only one is left.
So what happened to the other five?
Rewind about a hundred thousand years.
Africa, us, Homo sapiens.
Europe, the Neanderthals, short and stocky.
Siberia and East Asia, the Denisovans.
For years, all we had of them was a finger bone and a few teeth.
Hey, I'm more than a pinky!
Java, Indonesia, the last Homo erectus, a species that lasted nearly two million years.
The island of Flores, Homo floresiensis, about one meter tall, scientists call them the
hobbits.
We prefer fun-sized.
and the Philippines, Homo Lusonensis, only discovered in 2019.
Six kinds of humans, one planet.
So why is there only one now?
By about 40,000 years ago, the Neanderthals were gone.
One by one, the others vanished too.
Why?
Scientists are still arguing in very long papers.
But here's the twist.
They didn't vanish completely.
When our ancestors met them, they had babies.
If your family comes from Europe or Asia, about 1-2% of your DNA is Neanderthal.
In Papua New Guinea, it's up to about 5% Denisovan.
So, technically, we never laughed.
This is Boogal. Follow for more geography fun facts.
